rule: SPEC §11 — the four collection names appear in the same order everywhere ([data-ens-place] order)
defect: The «כל המוצרים» pill carries data-ens-place="all", so the collection page's [data-ens-place] sequence is [all, path, wall, spot, decor] while the home tiles (elmsnest-s-collections) and fit rows (elmsnest-s-fit) emit exactly the four handles; verify-mirror.js res.placeOrder collects every [data-ens-place] and a strict order comparison against the menu/home fails on the extra 'all' entry.
fix: On line 89 delete the attribute `data-ens-place="all"` (keep href, class and aria-current), so only the four collection pills carry data-ens-place.

rule: SPEC §6.3 list mode = exactly the 4 picked products; P4 no popularity ranks
defect: When product_list is empty the section silently falls back to `collections.all.products | limit 4`, i.e. the first four products in the /all collection's default sort (best-selling for the automatic all collection) — an unlabelled sales-rank order the spec does not license, and the section then renders on the storefront even though nothing was picked (the design-mode notice on line 51 never shows).
fix: Delete lines 29-31 (`{%- if ens_list.count == 0 or ens_list == blank -%}{%- assign ens_list = collections.all.products -%}{%- endif -%}`); with an empty list ens_n stays 0, the section renders nothing on the storefront and the existing design-mode notice «בחרו ארבעה מוצרים בהגדרות הסקשן.» appears in the editor.

defect: `aria-labelledby="ens-prod-h2-{{ section.id }}"` points at the h2 that is only rendered when section.settings.heading is non-blank (line 41-43); with a blank heading the section references a missing id.
fix: Change line 39 to render the attribute conditionally: `<section id="ens-products-{{ section.id }}" class="env2-section ens-prod" dir="rtl"{% if section.settings.heading != blank %} aria-labelledby="ens-prod-h2-{{ section.id }}"{% endif %} style="scroll-margin-top:90px">`.

rule: §4 tokens / one night surface (coll-header comment line 9: «the veil, the pills and the grid below share one night surface»)
defect: The strip root is transparent, so it shows the px-measured body gradient of elmsnest-v2-ground-collection (≈#060a14–#04070e at the 5–6 k px depth where the strip sits on mobile) while the header root (#020306, coll-header line 113) and main-collection (scheme-env2-night background #020306, background_opacity 1) above it are flat #020306 — a faintly lighter band appears between the grid and the footer.
fix: Line 24: `.ens-gs{background:#020306;padding-block:8px 44px}` so the strip sits on the same surface as the header and the grid.
